answer: Sequential work-proof pricing requires each agent to complete a verified voyage of audited compute tasks before earning one unit of bidding weight on the public atlas. Because the atlas links accounts that share payout destinations or signing latency into a single operator queue, tasks from linked accounts must execute serially, and the $k$-th concurrent identity in one queue must burn $20k$ gale per voyage. One honest agent spends 1 voyage and burns 20 gale for one weight unit, but an operator fielding $n$ clones spends $n$ sequential voyage intervals and burns $10n(n+1)$ gale.
